source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
Digging the hole: the planting hole should be a suitable size, about one meter deep, one meter long, and one meter wide (roughly a one-meter cube). Holes should be spaced at least about 8 meters apart, and arranged so the planting rows line up and each tree receives even sunlight. Note: the page's diagram shows a grid-spacing figure of 10 meters between trees, which does not exactly match the 8-meter minimum given in the body text — both numbers are reported here as they appear, since it was not possible to confirm from the scan which one is authoritative.

Putting soil in the hole: after digging the hole, and before planting, collect plant litter/debris, animal manure, or compost soil and put a generous amount into the hole. This is beneficial because it is natural material rich in nutrients. The illustration shows a farmer pouring a compost mixture (with labeled components including animal manure and compost soil) into a hole with a depth/width noted as about 1 meter.

Planting the seedling: inspect and handle the seedling carefully. The seedling should be at least two months old. Cut the bag open freshly with a sharp knife, taking care not to break apart the soil around the roots. Plant in the evening so the seedling can take in moisture overnight, and water it afterward so the roots settle into the new soil.
